note: SHRINK-ONLY, and EMPTY. One row per commit the object store GAINED beyond the base ref that carries an identity other than the branch's anchored one AND sits in a reach class a `git push --all` / `--tags` would publish. A `branch`-reach row is a SCHEMA ERROR, never a declaration: a foreign identity on the ref under review is the finding. Rows carry a sha, never an address -- the identity is anchored at runtime through the commit-series fixture's anchor and this file is committed (R-LOC-03). The ratchet bites both ways: an undeclared foreign commit in a gated class fails, and a row whose commit this store still HOLDS while no push would publish it fails as stale, naming itself. A row is INAPPLICABLE, never stale, where the commit is absent from the store entirely -- a clone, a CI checkout and the parity sweep's sandbox never receive a local backup ref.
cleared: 2026-08-20, task 83. The file was authored with three rows -- task 82's pre-rewrite tips, which carried the second personal address its rewrite removed from the branch and which sat on refs/heads/backup/task82-pre-identity-rewrite, the namespace `git push --all` publishes. Declaring them was the wrong instrument and running the gate proved it: a row keyed on ONE working copy's ref topology is stale in every clone (where the same ref arrives as refs/remotes/*, which is already safe), so the ratchet would have been red on CI and green only on the machine that wrote it. The invariant was made TRUE instead. The backup was mirrored to refs/backup/task82-pre-identity-rewrite -- same sha, a namespace no push publishes without an explicit refspec -- and the refs/heads/ spelling removed. Nothing was lost and it is reversible with one command: `git update-ref refs/heads/backup/task82-pre-identity-rewrite 49eeb2c9aa6b97b32eb56107bde57453433d8a2e`; refs/task82-original/refs/heads/merge/modularize independently holds the identical sha.
